review.summary: The patch fixes an incorrect dispatch condition in `Base.view` for `SArray`. The old code decided whether to wrap a view result in `Scalar` by comparing the result type against the array's element type (`_maybewrapscalar(S::SArray{<:Any,T}, r::T)`), which is only a proxy for 'the result is 0-dimensional'. That proxy misfires whenever the eltype is abstract (e.g. `Any`, `Number`), because then any result type matches `T` and non-scalar views get wrongly wrapped in `Scalar`. The fix keys the decision on `Base.index_dimsum(I...) === Tuple{}`, which is the actual criterion for a 0-dimensional (scalar) view. This is a behavior fix in production code, not a feature or refactor.
review.evidence: Single-hunk production change in src/abstractarray.jl replacing eltype-based dispatch with `Base.index_dimsum(I...)`-based dispatch; accompanying test change in test/indexing.jl; minimization reports the hunk is globally minimal and necessary; runtime evidence reports a stable differential over 3 repetitions with the full suite passing on the fixed revision. The pre-existing comment referencing issue #892 confirms the `Scalar` wrapping behavior was already intended for 0D views, so returning `Scalar` for a non-0D view violates existing intended behavior.

review.validation_risks: Traceability is UNVERIFIED, so the trigger test may not correspond to a named suite test; validation must rely on the dedicated differential script. Behavior depends on `Base.index_dimsum`, an internal Base function, so results can vary across Julia versions. Also, some previously-wrapped results (abstract-eltype arrays) change type, which could surface as failures elsewhere if other tests relied on the old wrapping.
review.suggested_tests: In test/indexing.jl: assert `view(SMatrix{2,2,Any}([1 2; 3 4]), :, 1) isa SVector` (not `Scalar`), and similarly for `Number`/`Real` eltypes; assert 0D views still wrap, e.g. `view(SMatrix{2,2,Int}(...), 1, 1) isa Scalar` and `view(SVector{3,Int}(...), 2) isa Scalar`; check mixed index kinds (`Colon`, `SOneTo`, `SVector{N,Int}`, `CartesianIndex`) produce results whose dimensionality matches `Base.index_dimsum`; compare against `parent`/values equality with the non-static `view` result.
